items.label: SHABBAT RETRIEVAL
items.hebrew: העני עומד בחוץ ובעל הבית בפנים
items.translation: The poor person stands outside and the homeowner inside.
items.prompt: Before deciding any category, what must you map in this opening case?
answers: The people, their locations, and the action crossing a boundary.
The final practical ruling without the case.
items.feedback: Right. In Shabbat’s opening, people and domains make the case intelligible.
items.sourceContext: Shabbat delayed retrieval: people and domains

items.label: PESACHIM RETRIEVAL
items.prompt: What reading move does this short Gemara question require?
answers: Pause over the contested word and ask how its meaning changes the case.
Skip the Mishnah and find a final ruling.
Treat the word as a person’s name.
items.feedback: Right. A compact word can carry the entire question in a sugya.

items.label: ERUVIN RETRIEVAL
items.hebrew: מבוי שהוא גבוה למעלה מעשרים אמה · ימעט
items.translation: An alleyway higher than twenty cubits: one should lower it.
items.prompt: What is the disciplined first map of this source?
answers: Object, measurement, response, then the reason the threshold matters.
Memorize twenty and ignore the alleyway.
Assume any measurement has the same purpose.
items.feedback: Right. The number only becomes meaningful inside its object, response, and reason.
items.sourceContext: Eruvin delayed retrieval: measure and reason

items.label: SUKKAH RETRIEVAL
items.hebrew: סוכה שהיא גבוהה למעלה מעשרים אמה · פסולה
items.translation: A sukkah higher than twenty cubits is invalid.
items.prompt: What should you seek after identifying this ruling?
answers: The reason and proof-text role that explain why the measure affects validity.
items.feedback: Right. The reading task is to trace ruling, reason, and source—not to treat the measure as isolated.
items.sourceContext: Sukkah delayed retrieval: ruling and source

items.label: BAVA METZIA RETRIEVAL
items.hebrew: שנים אוחזין בטלית · זה אומר אני מצאתיה · וזה אומר אני מצאתיה
items.translation: Two hold a garment; each says, “I found it.”
items.prompt: What must remain distinct before you assess the Mishnah’s response?
answers: The shared object, each claimant’s assertion, and any later evidence or response.
The two claims, because identical claims are automatically proof.
The object, because the people are only background.
items.feedback: Right. A claim is part of the case; it is not yet proof.
items.sourceContext: Bava Metzia delayed retrieval: claims and response

items.label: BAVA KAMMA RETRIEVAL
items.translation: The ox is not like the maveh.
items.prompt: Why does the Mishnah name a difference before giving a shared principle?
answers: To show that cases can share responsibility while remaining meaningfully distinct.
To prove that no categories can be compared.
To replace the opening category list.
items.feedback: Right. Classification requires both difference and a unifying principle.
items.sourceContext: Bava Kamma delayed retrieval: difference and principle
